speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} has elected a goose as treasurer. In fairness, the goose has never missed a meeting and has never once spent any money.

choices.label: Congratulate the goose.
choices.reaction: The goose receives a small brass nameplate. Donations to the {city} {assembly} triple. Nobody can explain the connection, and nobody tries.

choices.label: A treasurer should be a person.
choices.reaction: The goose is demoted to Vice Treasurer. The minutes record that it took the news well.

speaker: gary
text: The {city} {assembly} built a replica of my garage in their park. To scale. They even got the lawnmower right. I went to see it, and I think I’d kind of like to live in it.

choices.label: Gary can have a second garage.
choices.reaction: Gary moves into the replica on weekends. Tourists visit both garages and argue about which is the real one. Gary sleeps through the argument in each.

choices.label: One garage is plenty, Gary.
choices.reaction: Gary visits the replica every Sunday instead, and sits in the replica chair, which he says is more comfortable than the real one.

speaker: any
text: {city} has started its own newspaper, the {city} Daily Good News. It reports only on {city}, and only good news. Yesterday’s front page: LOCAL MAN STILL GREAT.

choices.label: Get it delivered to every member.
choices.reaction: Circulation reaches every member and several confused dentists’ offices. Morale rises everywhere the paper lands.

choices.label: Ask them to print some bad news too.
choices.reaction: The next edition reports, gravely, that it rained on Tuesday. Readers are shaken.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} has written a musical about you. Your character has a tap number in the second act. Opening night is Friday. They’ve saved you a seat in the front row, and a pair of tap shoes, just in case.

choices.label: Go, and bring the tap shoes.
choices.reaction: You are pulled onstage for the finale. You tap. It is not good. The audience gives it a standing ovation, which they insist afterward was sincere.

choices.label: Send flowers instead.
choices.reaction: The flowers get their own curtain call.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} has declared independence. Not from us: from the parking lot next door, which has been bothering them for years. They’d like your blessing, and a flag.

choices.label: Design them a flag.
choices.reaction: The flag shows a parking lot with a line through it. It is flown with enormous pride, mostly at the parking lot.

choices.label: We don’t really do flags.
choices.reaction: {city} makes its own flag anyway. It is the same flag, but larger.

speaker: any
text: {city} has commissioned a nine-foot bronze statue of Priya’s ladle. Priya asked me to tell you she is mortified. She also asked whether it could be ten feet.

choices.label: Ten feet.
choices.reaction: The ladle is unveiled at ten feet. Priya cries, and then says it’s the wind, and then cries again.

choices.label: Nine is plenty.
choices.reaction: Priya says nine is plenty, in the voice of someone who wanted ten.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} has added an extra {day} to the week. It falls after the usual {day} and before whatever comes next. Their calendars are now nine days long.

choices.label: Recognize the extra {day}.
choices.reaction: Other assemblies adopt the extra {day} within a month. The movement now runs on its own calendar, which nobody else can read.

choices.label: A week has seven days.
choices.reaction: {city} accepts this, then quietly keeps the nine-day calendar for birthdays.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} now offers degrees in {belief}. Three people have graduated. One of them is a professor now, and has started correcting you in public.

choices.label: Accept an honorary doctorate.
choices.reaction: You are now Doctor {title}. The professor attends the ceremony and corrects your pronunciation of your own name.

choices.label: Invite the professor to lunch.
choices.reaction: The professor talks about {belief} for three hours. You learn several things about yourself.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} is bigger than {hometown} now, and they want to throw your birthday party. They don’t know when your birthday is, so they picked one. It’s next {day}. It’s also going to be every {day}.

choices.label: Every week is my birthday now.
choices.reaction: You turn fifty-two times in a year. The cake budget becomes the movement’s largest line item.

choices.label: Once a year is plenty.
choices.reaction: {city} agrees, and throws the party once a year, for a week.

speaker: any
text: {city} has twinned itself with a town overseas that also does {belief}, but upside down. Their delegation arrives tomorrow. Nobody knows which way up to greet them.

choices.label: Greet them upside down.
choices.reaction: Handstands all around. The delegation is moved to tears. Some of the tears run upward.

choices.label: Right side up, and hope for the best.
choices.reaction: The delegation is too polite to mention it. They do everything upside down for the rest of the visit, to make you feel at home.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} held an election for Founder. You weren’t running. You came in second, to a man named Phil, who also wasn’t running. Phil would like to know what he’s supposed to do now.

choices.label: Make Phil the Founder of {city}.
choices.reaction: Phil founds {city} again, from scratch, in the same building. Attendance doubles.

choices.label: There’s only one founder.
choices.reaction: Phil is relieved. He goes back to running the hardware store, where he is, everyone agrees, a natural leader.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} started forecasting the weather according to {belief}. They’ve been right eleven days in a row. The actual weather service called to ask how.

choices.label: Tell them our secret.
choices.reaction: The weather service adopts the method for a trial week. It rains on the right days. A meteorologist joins.

choices.label: A good magician never tells.
choices.reaction: The forecasts continue. The weather service starts quietly checking them before going on air.

speaker: gary
text: I fell asleep in the big church in {city} during the tour. When I woke up there was a second tour, about me. The guide says I’m the most peaceful thing they’ve had in years.

choices.label: Gary is a local landmark now.
choices.reaction: Gary is added to the official tour, between the stained glass and the gift shop. He is, by all reports, the highlight.

choices.label: Gary, maybe sleep somewhere less famous.
choices.reaction: Gary moves to a quieter church. A smaller tour forms around him there too.

speaker: gary
text: {city} has a hammock store. I’ve been testing hammocks for six days. The owner made me an offer: a free hammock, if I keep lying in the front window. People stop and watch. Several have joined.

choices.label: Take the deal.
choices.reaction: Gary becomes {city}’s most popular window display. The hammock store hosts the {assembly} meetings now, lying down.

choices.label: Buy the hammock. Gary comes home.
choices.reaction: Gary comes home with the hammock and hangs it in the garage. It becomes a site of pilgrimage within the month.

speaker: gary
text: A dog has followed me around {city} for three days. I think he’s a member now. He comes to the {meeting} and lies down at exactly the right moments.

choices.label: Give the dog a name badge.
choices.reaction: The dog’s name badge says MEMBER. He wears it with tremendous dignity and is elected to the welcome committee.

choices.label: Find the dog’s owner.
choices.reaction: The owner turns out to be the mayor, who also joins, mostly to keep an eye on the dog.

speaker: priya
text: I made soup for a wedding in {city}. The wrong wedding. A different wedding. They loved it anyway, the bride has joined, and the groom would like to know what he’s joined.

choices.label: Welcome the whole wedding.
choices.reaction: The entire wedding party joins, including a cake that the bride insists counts. The groom is still finding out what he’s joined, and enjoying it.

choices.label: Find the right wedding and apologize.
choices.reaction: The right wedding gets soup too, a day late. They join out of sympathy.

speaker: priya
text: The mayor of {city} came for soup and stayed for six hours. He cried twice. He wants to make {belief} the official soup of {city}, which isn’t how soup works, but here we are.

choices.label: Let him make it official.
choices.reaction: The proclamation is read from the town hall steps. Several people point out that {belief} is not a soup. The mayor says it is now.

choices.label: Suggest a regular soup.
choices.reaction: The official soup of {city} is now lentil. The mayor still comes every week, and still cries, just once now.

speaker: dez
text: I rented a blimp. It says {movement} on the side, and it’s over {city} right now. I didn’t know blimps don’t really steer. It’s over the next county now. People in the next county are very excited.

choices.label: Let the blimp go where it goes.
choices.reaction: The blimp drifts across four counties in two days. Membership rises along its route, like a very slow parade.

choices.label: Bring the blimp down.
choices.reaction: The blimp lands in a cornfield. The farmer joins. The cows remain undecided.

speaker: dez
text: I told {city} we’d break the world record for the most people doing {belief} at the same time. They already booked the football stadium. We need four thousand people by Saturday.

choices.label: Fill the stadium.
choices.reaction: Four thousand two hundred people turn up. The record is broken. The record people admit they had to create a new category to break.

choices.label: Book a smaller venue.
choices.reaction: The record attempt moves to a bowling alley. You break the bowling-alley record instead. It is framed.

speaker: dez
text: The mayor of {city} gave me the key to the city. It turns out it opens an actual door, to the {city} water tower. I’m in the water tower now. The view is incredible. Can we start a chapter up here?

choices.label: A chapter in the water tower.
choices.reaction: The Water Tower Chapter meets weekly, sixty feet up. Membership is limited by the number of people who can climb a ladder, and grows anyway.

choices.label: Come down, Dez.
choices.reaction: Dez comes down, slowly, waving the whole way. A crowd has gathered. Some of them join.

speaker: martin
text: {city} has never had a block party. I’ve organized one. There are name badges, a bounce house and a seating plan for the bounce house.

choices.label: Make it an annual event.
choices.reaction: The {city} block party becomes the event of the summer. The bounce house seating plan is laminated and framed at town hall.

choices.label: Maybe lose the seating plan.
choices.reaction: Without the seating plan, the bounce house descends into joyful chaos. Martin watches from a folding chair, laminating his feelings.

speaker: martin
text: The {city} {assembly} has a karaoke night. I sang. Now they want me to sing at every meeting. I don’t know how to say no to a standing ovation, {title}.

choices.label: Martin sings.
choices.reaction: Martin’s rendition of a power ballad becomes a weekly tradition in {city}. People drive in from three towns to hear it.

choices.label: Once is legendary. Twice is a habit.
choices.reaction: Martin agrees, and sings it once more, at the door, on the way out. It is even better.

speaker: juniper
text: I filmed the {city} members doing {belief} and posted it. It has eleven million views. Most of the comments are from people in other countries asking whether they can join from there.

choices.label: Say yes to all of them.
choices.reaction: Overnight, {movement} has members on four continents, most of whom have only seen one video and are completely committed.

choices.label: One country at a time.
choices.reaction: Juniper pins a comment: “Soon.” It gets more likes than the video.

speaker: rolf
text: {city} had a parking problem. I solved it: I bought the parking lot. We now own a parking lot. It is extremely profitable, and nobody is sure whether it is in keeping with {belief}.

choices.label: Keep the parking lot.
choices.reaction: The {movement} parking lot becomes the most cheerful parking lot in the state. The attendant hands out soup.

choices.label: Turn it into a park.
choices.reaction: The parking lot becomes a park. The park becomes a meeting place. Rolf visits it, slightly mournfully, and counts the benches.

speaker: dispatched
text: The kids in {city} have started doing {belief} at recess. The school wrote to ask whether it’s educational. The principal has started joining in.

choices.label: Offer to visit the school.
choices.reaction: You visit. The kids teach you a version of {belief} more advanced than yours. Parents join to find out what their children are talking about.

choices.label: Let recess be recess.
choices.reaction: Recess continues. A teacher reports that {belief} has replaced tag entirely.

speaker: dispatched
text: Small problem. There are two towns called {city}, and I think I’m in the other one. The other one has been very welcoming. Should I start a branch here anyway?

choices.label: Start one in both.
choices.reaction: {movement} now has a {city} branch and a Second {city} branch. They meet once a year to argue about which is which.

choices.label: Come back to the right {city}.
choices.reaction: They come back. The wrong {city} sends a fruit basket and a membership application.

speaker: bev
text: We have a rush hour now, hon. Every {day} at six, nine hundred members try to leave {hometown} for the same three towns. I’ve put on extra buses. I’ve also put on a man with a whistle.

choices.label: More buses.
choices.reaction: The buses run every ten minutes. The man with the whistle becomes a minor celebrity and asks for a second whistle.

choices.label: Stagger the {meeting} times.
choices.reaction: The {meeting} now starts at six, six-fifteen and six-thirty, depending on your last name. Bev considers it her finest work.

speaker: bev
text: I’ve lost Gary. Not lost lost: I know he’s on the number 12. The number 12 doesn’t stop until the coast. He’ll be fine. He’ll be on the coast.

choices.label: Start a beach chapter while he’s there.
choices.reaction: Gary wakes up on the coast and, by the time the return bus arrives, has founded the Beach Chapter. It meets lying down, on towels.

choices.label: Send a car for Gary.
choices.reaction: The car finds Gary asleep on a bench facing the ocean. He says it was the best trip of his life, and he’d like to go again, awake.

speaker: bev
text: My old bus depot wants to throw me a retirement party. I retired eleven years ago. They just noticed I wasn’t there. Can I take the afternoon?

choices.label: Take the whole day, Bev.
choices.reaction: Bev goes to her party and comes back with forty bus drivers, all members, all on time.

choices.label: Can it wait until after {day}?
choices.reaction: Bev says it’s waited eleven years, it can wait a week. It does. She goes. The drivers join anyway.

speaker: any
text: We have ten thousand members. Someone made a cake in the shape of everybody. It took nine bakeries. Where do we put it?

choices.label: Cut it. Everyone gets a piece of everyone.
choices.reaction: The cake is cut at a ceremony that runs four hours. Somebody gets Gary’s head. They frame the plate.

choices.label: Preserve it.
choices.reaction: The cake goes on display. It does not keep. The display becomes something else, and then a tourist attraction.

speaker: any
text: Our quarter-millionth member just joined. Her name is Doris, and she thought she was entering a raffle. She’d like her prize.

choices.label: Give Doris a prize.
choices.reaction: Doris wins a lifetime supply of soup, a parade and a small bronze plaque. She becomes the most enthusiastic member the movement has ever had.

choices.label: Explain to Doris what she’s joined.
choices.reaction: Doris listens to the whole explanation, says “Huh,” and stays anyway. She still asks about the raffle every week.

speaker: any
text: A theme park company wants to build {Movement}land. There would be a ride called “{belief}: The Experience.” Gary asked whether there would be a quiet room. There would not.

choices.label: Build it, with a quiet room.
choices.reaction: {Movement}land opens with a roller coaster, a soup flume and, in the middle, one very quiet room. Gary’s room has the longest line in the park.

choices.label: We are not a theme park.
choices.reaction: The company builds a rival park instead. It is called Movementland, without the name, and nobody goes.

speaker: any
text: One million members. The millionth is a dog. His owner signed him up as a joke, but he has come to every {meeting} since, and he sits in the front row.

choices.label: Throw the dog a parade.
choices.reaction: The parade route is lined with half a million people and several thousand dogs, all of whom are now members.

choices.label: A quiet ceremony. He’s a good dog.
choices.reaction: The dog is given a medal on a ribbon. He sleeps through the ceremony, which members agree is the most on-brand thing that could have happened.

speaker: any
text: The postal service wants to put {belief} on a stamp. They need a picture. Martin has submitted forty-one. Dez has submitted one, of himself.

choices.label: Use Martin’s best one.
choices.reaction: The stamp sells out in a day. Collectors pay a fortune for the misprinted version, which shows Martin’s thumb.

choices.label: Use Dez’s.
choices.reaction: The stamp shows Dez, beaming, holding a megaphone. Letters arrive everywhere with a slightly louder feel to them.

speaker: any
text: There are now more of us than there are people in several countries. One of those countries wrote to us, slightly nervously, to ask what our intentions are.

choices.label: Send them soup.
choices.reaction: The soup arrives in a diplomatic pouch. The country writes back to say it is reassured, and could it have the recipe.

choices.label: Tell them our intentions are unclear, even to us.
choices.reaction: The country is not reassured, but it is charmed. Its prime minister joins.

speaker: any
text: Members abroad want a {movement} passport. It wouldn’t get you into any country. It would get you into every {meeting}, anywhere, and a free bowl of soup.

choices.label: Issue the passports.
choices.reaction: The passport is navy blue, with a ladle on the cover. Border guards in four countries ask how to apply.

choices.label: A membership card is enough.
choices.reaction: The membership card gets a small airplane printed on it. Everyone agrees it counts.

speaker: any
text: We need {belief} translated into forty languages. In nine of them it comes out as something else entirely. In one, it’s apparently a kind of sandwich.

choices.label: Embrace the sandwich.
choices.reaction: In that country the movement is now mostly about sandwiches. It is our fastest-growing branch.

choices.label: Hire better translators.
choices.reaction: The new translations are perfect, and much less popular than the sandwich.

speaker: gary
text: I’ve been to six countries this month. I slept through all of them. I woke up as a member of three local movements that aren’t ours. They seem nice.

choices.label: Make them sister movements.
choices.reaction: The three movements become sister organizations. Their founders write to Gary every month. He replies, eventually, from a hammock.

choices.label: Gary should stay home for a while.
choices.reaction: Gary stays home for a month and sleeps in his own garage. He says it’s the best country he’s been to.

speaker: priya
text: Two countries that don’t speak to each other both came to my soup tent at the border. They’re sitting at the same table. They haven’t said a word to each other, but they asked for seconds at exactly the same time.

choices.label: Keep the tent open. Forever.
choices.reaction: The tent becomes a permanent fixture. Diplomats start scheduling meetings there because the soup is better than at the embassies.

choices.label: Seat them at separate tables.
choices.reaction: They move to separate tables, then move back, because the separate tables are farther from the pot.

speaker: dez
text: I may have promised a continent. Not all of it. The bigger half.

choices.label: Then we’d better get going.
choices.reaction: Dez maps out the bigger half with a marker and a lot of confidence. The buses leave at dawn.

choices.label: Unpromise the continent.
choices.reaction: Dez apologizes to the continent, by video. The continent takes it well.

speaker: any
text: We’ve been invited to the International Song Contest. Every country sends one song. We aren’t a country. They’ve let us in anyway, because nobody could find a rule against it.

choices.label: Juniper writes the song.
choices.reaction: The song is about {belief} and has nine key changes. It comes second, behind a country that sent a man in a suit made of mirrors.

choices.label: Martin sings the power ballad.
choices.reaction: Martin sings. The arena sings back. We win, technically, on a recount nobody asked for.

speaker: any
text: A country has offered us an embassy. It’s a two-bedroom apartment above a bakery. It has a flagpole. It does not have a flag.

choices.label: Accept, and make a flag.
choices.reaction: The flag shows a garage door. The bakery downstairs starts making garage-shaped bread.

choices.label: Turn it into a soup kitchen.
choices.reaction: The embassy serves soup to anyone who asks. It is the most visited embassy in the city by a long way.

speaker: martin
text: There’s a man in another country who does exactly what I do. Same clipboards. Same laminator. Same feelings about name badges. We’ve been writing. I think I’ve met my match, {title}, and I don’t know whether to be thrilled or furious.

choices.label: Invite him to visit.
choices.reaction: The two Martins meet at the airport. They laminate each other’s boarding passes. They have been inseparable ever since.

choices.label: Keep it to letters.
choices.reaction: The letters get longer and more competitive. Martin starts color-coding them. So does the other Martin.

speaker: bev
text: The movement now spans eleven time zones, hon. It is always {day} somewhere. Somebody is always at a {meeting}. I haven’t slept since Thursday, but the buses are running.

choices.label: Hire Bev two deputies.
choices.reaction: Bev hires two retired dispatchers, one for each half of the world. They run the schedule in shifts and send each other postcards.

choices.label: Bev, go to bed.
choices.reaction: Bev goes to bed for fourteen hours. The schedule runs itself, almost perfectly. She is quietly furious about the almost.

speaker: any
text: A movement abroad is exactly like ours, except they started with naps where we started with {belief}. Their founder wants to meet. He suggested a neutral country. He also suggested a nap.

choices.label: Meet, and nap.
choices.reaction: The two founders nap side by side in a neutral country. The photograph is the most peaceful image of the year.

choices.label: Meet, but stay awake.
choices.reaction: You stay awake. He sleeps. The meeting goes very well from his side.

speaker: any
text: The International Assembly of Nations asked whether {movement} is a country, a religion, a club or a weather system. Their form has only one box.

choices.label: Check “weather system.”
choices.reaction: We are officially classified as a weather system. Several countries issue advisories. Membership rises in all of them.

choices.label: Write in “a group of friends.”
choices.reaction: The form is rejected for writing outside the box. A clerk joins anyway.

speaker: gary
text: The lawnmower has become a member. Not officially. People just keep saying hello to it on the way in. Somebody put a name tag on it. It says LARRY.

choices.label: Larry is a member.
choices.reaction: Larry is given a seat in the front row. Attendance improves, though nobody will admit it’s because of Larry.

choices.label: It’s a lawnmower, Gary.
choices.reaction: Gary agrees it’s a lawnmower. Larry’s name tag stays on, though, out of respect.

speaker: dez
text: Someone on the next street started their own garage meeting. They copied everything. They even have a Gary. Their Gary is awake.

choices.label: Challenge them to a bake-off.
choices.reaction: The bake-off ends in a draw and a merger. Their Gary and our Gary meet. Ours falls asleep. Theirs, inspired, does too.

choices.label: Imitation is flattery.
choices.reaction: You send them a fruit basket. They copy the fruit basket.

speaker: priya
text: Somebody brought a casserole. Not soup. A casserole. People are uneasy. I don’t want to be territorial, but I’m going to be a little territorial.

choices.label: Casseroles are welcome too.
choices.reaction: The casserole is a hit. Priya tries it, says “fine,” and asks for the recipe in a very small voice.

choices.label: This is a soup movement.
choices.reaction: The casserole is gently redirected to the bake sale table, where it sells out in four minutes.

speaker: martin
text: The bowling alley has offered us Thursday nights. Everyone gets custom shirts. I designed them. They’re beautiful. They say {movement} on the back and BOWL WITH PURPOSE on the front.

choices.label: Bowl with purpose.
choices.reaction: The league is a triumph. Nobody can bowl. The shirts are so popular that people who have never bowled order them.

choices.label: Maybe just the shirts.
choices.reaction: The shirts become the unofficial uniform. Several members bowl in them anyway, on their own, for the look.

speaker: dez
text: I called in to a late-night radio show to talk about {belief}. I’ve been on for four hours. They won’t let me leave. Their ratings are the highest they’ve ever had.

choices.label: Stay on until dawn.
choices.reaction: Dez stays on until sunrise. Half the town has heard of {movement} by breakfast. The other half was asleep and is annoyed to have missed it.

choices.label: Hang up and go to bed, Dez.
choices.reaction: Dez hangs up. The station plays his last sentence on a loop for an hour, because nobody can find the off switch.

speaker: any
text: Members staged a surprise {belief} in the {hometown} mall. It was so surprising that the security guards joined in. The mall manager wants to know if we do birthdays.

choices.label: We do birthdays now.
choices.reaction: Members are booked for eleven birthdays, a bar mitzvah and a retirement party. All the guests join.

choices.label: We do surprises, not bookings.
choices.reaction: The flash mob strikes again at the bus station, the library and, once, a dentist’s office. Nobody ever knows where next.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} now ends every {meeting} with a group hug that lasts exactly four minutes. Someone brings an egg timer.
variants: The {city} {assembly} now ends every {meeting} with a group hug that lasts exactly four minutes. Someone brings an egg timer.
In {city}, members have started greeting each other by saying the movement’s name backward. It has caught on. Nobody can pronounce it.
The {city} {assembly} has adopted a mascot: a raccoon that lives behind the hall. The raccoon has not been consulted.
{city} members now wear one sock inside out on {day}s, as a sign of commitment. Nobody remembers who started it. Gary suspects it was him.
The {city} {assembly} has started holding its {meetings} in a laundromat, for the warmth and the rhythm of the dryers.
In {city}, it is now customary to bring a houseplant to your first {meeting}. The hall has become a jungle. Visitors get lost.
The {city} {assembly} has replaced applause with a polite, synchronized whistle. The dogs in the neighborhood have strong feelings about it.
Members in {city} now sign every email with a small drawing of a {beliefNoun}. Their employers have started asking questions.
The {city} {assembly} sings the minutes instead of reading them. The minutes have never been more popular, or less accurate.
In {city}, the oldest member wears a crown at every {meeting}. It is made of cardboard. It is also, they insist, sacred.

choices.label: Spread it to every assembly.
choices.reaction: Within a month, every assembly does it. {city} is unbearably proud, and says so in a newsletter nobody asked for.

choices.label: That’s a {city} thing.
choices.reaction: {city} keeps it to themselves, and becomes the place people visit to see it done properly.

speaker: any
text: The {city} {assembly} would like a hot tub. For the members. For morale. They have a quote and a brochure.
variants: The {city} {assembly} would like a hot tub. For the members. For morale. They have a quote and a brochure.
{city} wants to send a delegation to every other assembly by tandem bicycle. They have twelve tandems. They need forty.
The {city} {assembly} wants a highway billboard that just says HI. They think it will work. Dez thinks it will work.
{city} is asking for a budget for a parade float. The float is a giant {beliefNoun}. It has a working fountain.
The {city} {assembly} has asked for a pipe organ. Nobody in {city} can play the organ. They say that’s what lessons are for.
{city} would like to adopt a mile of highway. They have already named it the {Movement} Mile, and they sweep it at midnight.
The {city} {assembly} wants to rent a lighthouse. There is no ocean anywhere near {city}. They found a lighthouse anyway.
{city} asks whether it can host a summer camp for members’ grandmothers. Forty grandmothers have signed up. They’ve made T-shirts.

choices.label: Fund it.
choices.hint: Costs money · They love you for it
choices.reaction: It arrives within the week. {city} holds a small ceremony, then a larger one, then a third to celebrate the first two.

choices.label: Not this year.
choices.reaction: {city} takes it well, and starts a bake sale to pay for it themselves. The bake sale becomes its own tradition.
